subject: maths
title: Measurement
description: Length, mass, capacity, perimeter, money including giving change, and time on analogue and digital clocks.

objectives.statement: Measure, compare, add and subtract: lengths (m/cm/mm); mass (kg/g); volume/capacity (l/ml).
Measure the perimeter of simple 2-D shapes.
Add and subtract amounts of money to give change, using both £ and p in practical contexts.
Tell and write the time from an analogue clock, including using Roman numerals from I to XII, and 12-hour and 24-hour clocks.

Estimate and read time with increasing accuracy to the nearest minute; record and compare time in terms of seconds, minutes and hours; use vocabulary such as o'clock, a.m./p.m., morning, afternoon, noon and midnight.
Know the number of seconds in a minute and the number of days in each month, year and leap year; compare durations of events.

items.prompt: How many centimetres are in 1 metre?
How many millimetres are in 1 centimetre?
Which of these is the longest?
A ribbon is 1 m 20 cm long. How many centimetres is that?
A square has sides of 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
A rectangle is 8 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter?

items.statement: Perimeter is the distance all the way around the outside of a shape.

items.prompt: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
Which of these is the heaviest?

items.statement: 1500 ml is the same as one and a half litres.

items.prompt: You buy a snack for 65p and pay with a £1 coin. How much change do you get?
A pencil costs 45p and a ruler costs 80p. What is the total cost?
A comic costs £1.30. You pay with a £2 coin. What is your change?
How many seconds are in one minute?
How many minutes are in one hour?
On a clock face with Roman numerals, what number does XII stand for?

items.statement: 15:00 on a 24-hour clock is 3 o'clock in the afternoon.

items.prompt: How many days are in a leap year?
Which of these months has exactly 30 days?

items.statement: A door is about 2 metres tall.
